task.description:
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED Step 1b (see handoffs/WF02-REQ168-20260828/step-01b-code-design-validator.json for the full verdict) on one BLOCKER finding.

BLOCKER: your design's section 1.1 claims (live-verified, quoted): `Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory) #=> {:ok, 65536}`. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently reproduced the identical call against the identical installed dependency (wasmex 0.15.1) and got the BARE INTEGER `65536` back -- not a tagged tuple. `{:ok, size} = Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory)` raises a MatchError. This is confirmed both by live reproduction and by deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/memory.ex:78's own @spec, which declares `pos_integer()` as the return type, not `{:ok, pos_integer()}`.

The good news: your design's ACTUAL algorithm (section 2, step 2: `memory_size = Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory)`) already uses the bare-integer form correctly -- this is purely a documentation-accuracy defect in section 1.1's transcript, not a defect in the design's own logic or the eventual implementation's correctness. But it is exactly the class of error section 1.6 of your own document warns against one section later (do not trust a claim about wasmex's return shape without live-verifying it) -- and it undermines confidence in section 1's other claims if left uncorrected, since section 1 explicitly states 'every other section's safety claim rests on section 1's findings, not on wasmex's published docs.'

Fix required: correct section 1.1's transcript to show the real, bare-integer return value (`Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory) #=> 65536`), and re-verify (live, yourself, do not just trust the validator's report) every other live-call transcript in section 1 (1.2 through 1.5) actually matches what the real installed dependency returns -- re-run each probe fresh rather than assuming only 1.1 was wrong. If any other transcript needs correction, fix it and note what changed. Do not weaken or remove the SIGABRT/hang findings (1.4) -- those were independently reproduced and confirmed correct by the validator; only 1.1's return-shape claim was wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Section 1.1 corrected to show the real, bare-integer return value of Wasmex.Memory.size/2, verified live yourself in this rework.

Every other live-call transcript in section 1 (1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5) re-verified live by you in this rework session, not merely trusted from the original draft -- state explicitly that you re-ran each one and confirm no other discrepancy exists, or fix any found.

The design's actual algorithm (section 2) and public contract (section 4) are re-checked for consistency with the corrected section 1.1 -- confirm no code path anywhere in the design assumes a tagged-tuple return from Wasmex.Memory.size/2.

All other content (section 2's arithmetic argument, section 3's module-location decision, section 5's test strategy, section 6's moduledoc, section 7's open questions, section 8's traceability table) already passed the validator's gate -- do not needlessly rewrite sections that were not flagged.
Zero literal Elixir code in the design doc, still true after the fix.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

Before making the edit, re-ran every other live-call transcript in section 1 myself, fresh, on the identical installed wasmex 0.15.1 dependency (PATH including .asdf/shims + .cargo/bin, WASMEX_BUILD=true) rather than trusting the original draft or the validator's spot-checks: (1.1) `Wasmex.Memory.size/2` confirmed to return the bare integer 65536, not a tuple -- scratch/rework1_probe_1_1_to_1_3.exs; (1.2) in-bounds set_byte/get_byte round-trip confirmed (7 back); (1.3) all 9 moderate-out-of-range rows re-run and every one returned the exact documented `{:error, "out of bounds memory access"}`, no crash; (1.4 Shape B) the length=2^40 SIGABRT re-run as an isolated `timeout 30 mix run --no-start` subprocess per the safety precaution -- real exit code 134, stderr 'memory allocation of 1099511627776 bytes failed', confirmed identical to the design's claim (scratch/rework1_probe_sigabrt.exs); (1.4 Shape A) the length=2^63 hang also re-run as an isolated `timeout 20 mix run --no-start` subprocess -- the call never returned, timeout killed it (exit 124) after the same 'capacity overflow' Rust panic message, confirming the hang claim too (scratch/rework1_probe_hang.exs); (1.5) two independent Wasmex.start_link/1 instances of identical bytes re-run -- write via instance A's handle, instance B reads back 0, instance A still reads 99, confirming isolation. Only section 1.1 required a correction; 1.2 through 1.5 all reproduced exactly as originally documented. Re-checked section 2 (arithmetic) and section 4 (public contract) line-by-line for any remaining assumption of a tagged-tuple return from Wasmex.Memory.size/2 -- none found; section 2 step 2 and section 4's check_bounds/3 doc both already use the bare-integer form. No other section (3, 5, 6, 7, 8) was rewritten -- only section 1's header note and section 1.1 itself were touched. Zero literal Elixir code remains (only one defmodule/end pair at lines 307/366 wrapping @type/@doc/@spec declarations, verified via grep).
